Its per-file vu32 clear helper was a copy of ZeroFill8; calling the shared (now CpuFill32-based) helper matches.

The ROM reloads gGameState before each store, which struct-field stores never do (in_struct alias rule); storing through a pointer parameter of a small inline setter gives the reload without raw offsets.
The mask/mode helpers took a shared mask parameter; writing each as its own predicate with the 0x3c00 constant inside and a named mode local let loop.c hoist only the shared mask, as the ROM does.
One table/mask swap: the table pseudo's REG_EQUIV doubling (AGBCC_NOEQUIV=table matches); the halves union that removes it in RandomizeMovement stays live from entry here and does not fold.

The random table is the integer RANDOM_TABLE_ADDR in one shared inline, so reload loads it and its rotation puts table, 0x618 and 0x674 in the ROM registers; rig->state read directly at each test splits the load/copy pseudos.
SetFlags/HasFlag helpers beside ClearFlags fix the operand ties; reading previousParameter in both arms of the delta wrap (jump2 merges them) gives slot the extra ref that wins r4 from flags.

Per-arm id compares fix the registers (id 5 refs) but jump2 cross-jumps the collider tail into the actor copy, the reverse of the ROM; the shared-compare goto form has the layout but id loses r3 (needs +2484).

EnableMotionFlags as a 16-bit bitfield |= gives the insert zero (r6) and lets combine sink the or after it; IsDown taking the u16 *flags pointer makes its 0x40 test an HImode load that cse replaces with the stored or-result, so case 1 reuses r2 with no reload.
Byte-identical twin of ResetActorState; the same C under its name matches.

The call argument is orb = &m->orbs[i] while p (state, fields) and position stay explicit pointers; orb is assigned again by the natural tail loop (orb = &m->orbs[i]; orb->sprite.flags |= 1), so loop.c no longer treats it as a replaceable giv and its copy into r1 stays before the test.

One flags pointer shared by both show loops (live past loop 1, so loop.c keeps it a separate biv instead of rewriting it as primary+8); the secondary hide arm reads widget = secondary so gcse sees two different +8 expressions and does not hoist them above the loops; per-arm hide pointer and mask; offset declared before digit to win the priority tie for r7.

Plain C with the real fields (collider.unknown3C/responseParameter, shadowStatus, state, index); the size helper as `return *field ? *field : 1;` reads the field twice, which puts the address in r1 as in the ROM.

Shared PlayerCue_StepSequenceEnded with sprite/sequence/entered locals (as TickPausing), a Jitter inline with u32 params and `center -= 48` as its own statement (no 0xFFD0), the second palette call via sprite; the last swap was global.c taking r6 from the doubled-life table (3/42) for the frames address (3/36): writing the z axis through `u16 sample; s16 center; s16 result` locals adds 6 flow-time extensions after the table dies, the frames address reaches 3/42 and goes to ip as in the ROM.

Per-branch ClearBits + return 1 (no shared mask pseudo, so post-reload cross-jumping makes the ROM tail and the constants land in r0); SetState with u8 params puts the zero after the 0x2A8 address; the plain fieldAA = (s32)fieldA8 copy; the last piece was actor tying STACK_REG 40 vs LO 42 in regclass: writing the 0x80 and 0x100 callback branches separately, each with its own Callback_InvokeActor (cross-jumped into one after reload), adds one LO-leaning arg copy and actor goes to r5.

The hundreds slot is a copy in r1 that the arms use while gcse still shares base<<1 with the glyph call: cse1 keeps the copy, gcse cprop turns the arms back into base (so PRE shares the shift), and cse2 flips them to the copy only when the copy outlives base (make_regs_eqv), so `row = base` before the hundreds call plus a dead `row++` at the end; reusing the row parameter gives the r1 preference from its entry copy; SetDigitVisible returns ++idx for the tens copy.

agbcc PRE (old LCM, DELAY a minimal fixpoint) hoists every outer-loop i + 1 above an inner loop; only a set of i inside the inner loop (or in the block just before its header) stops it, and a copy from a second variable leaves two pseudos that global.c will not put together in r8, so the bubble swap rewrites i as i + index - index: cse1 keeps it, gcse sees the kill, combine folds it to nothing.

No return statement (the caller reads the last call's r0, so the status pins go); per-block locals for mode/found/magnitude/direction and one u32 value; case 1 keeps gRandomTable in a variable and reads the second sample through the shared PARTICLE_RANDOM_READ_SAMPLE macro, whose loop notes double its refs so it gets r4 before the 1023 mask; case 1 stores baseDelay directly (a HImode copy) so jump2 cross-jumps only the random arm into case 2's, not the plain arm.

The ROM reloads the fields after the range test because the steering code is a two-entry label cse cannot follow: writing the end-of-trail statements in both failure paths (jump2 merges them) removes the memory barrier, and reading trail->target twice gives the r1-to-r3 copy.
Plain field sums match once the X margin is (s16)(shakeStrength + 42) between screen.x and shakeX (expansion and combine order give the ROM loads), and alternateLayer is an s16 (ldrsh test).

The barrier is gone once the actor pointer loses the r4 contest to active by live length: ShouldReact takes a u16 value and tests its two conditions in separate ifs, and MotionFlag takes a u8 mask (each adds pre-combine insns to the pointer's life, 94 to 101); the context is a SceneActorRegistryResetView, so the raw offsets become field67C and flags6D4.

Rewritten as plain field code with Chase_SetCtl/Chase_SetBehavior after an ordinary while loop: PRE hoists the store addresses above the loop, and its slot order needs a 65-bucket gcse table (129 insns, from a u16 temporary for the flag bit and one for responseValue); the head clears the motion flags through a MotionFlags(p) address helper and the tail through an actor helper, so cse2 makes the tail address a copy (the ROM r8).
A plain ?: optionalValue shortens the pre-combine lives so &pos outranks b, and CpuFill32 inside an inline helper places the control word last; no pins, barrier or volatile local.

Rewritten as plain C with the view struct as the parameter (header prototype; one pseudo instead of input+copy), channels read through the u16 pointer (fact 37), indexed target/destination in the sprite loop so loop.c pointers outrank the hoisted masks, and the bank offsets as separate statements (sub_08057CB8 style) giving the gcse table size for the spill order.

The table copy's r2 preference flowed through the block 2 address into the sway result; reusing one address variable for the distance read and the table lookup makes them conflict and breaks the chain, and block 1 stores its result back into wave.

Rewritten after TickPrimarySprites with the shared StepSprite inline: amplitude as i*4+24 (a reduced giv, set up after the hoisted 255), literal & 255, and three two-member unions for the values the ROM pairs in r2, r3 and r4.

Register pin removed and the random reads rewritten in TickWandering's style; one asm barrier on the table pointer remains, because without it the table's constant equivalence doubles its live length and the mask outranks it for r4 (AGBCC_NOEQUIV=table matches).

An indexed for loop over the 48 particles gives the ROM's two strength-reduced pointers, hoisted bit constants and reversed counter, and a separate state pointer keeps gcse from merging the flag reloads; all 11 pins and barriers removed.
Plain field assignments; the third ResetResponseState argument is a function-scope local so reload rematerializes it at the call (AGBCC_NOREG on the precomputed pseudo confirmed it).
switch on category, indexed destination, delta-then-base order, and an activeFlag variable set before the loop so the hoisted 0x2000 is rematerialized like the ROM.
u8 component variables add pre-combine zero_extend insns inside the loop, lengthening every loop-spanning live range so weight (short range) outranks the doubled-life componentMask constant.
